messages:
maya: FYI seeing huge capacity mismatch in eu-central — autoscaler reports 0 GPUs available but node pool shows 12 healthy GPU nodes. metrics for gpu-util and node-exporter are blank between 10:02-10:25 UTC. requests are piling in queue, not failing over to other regions :warning:
evian: confirming — queues spiking and router isn't shifting traffic. health checks for inference-gateway are flapping but k8s node status is Ready. could be an observability blindspot, not actual node loss
aria: i can confirm prometheus graphs are empty for that window. our scrape logs show repeated timeouts to metrics-proxy and then "context deadline exceeded" from kubelet endpoints. no traces captured for control-plane components during the window
liam: checked kube-system events — prometheus-sidecar restarted ~10:01 after OOMKilled. looks like a bursting metrics scrape got the sidecar memory spike. sidecar crash took down scrape pipeline and the autoscaler relies on those metrics
maya: logs from metrics-proxy: ```2026-03-17T10:01:05Z metrics-proxy ERROR tls handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2026-03-17T10:02:11Z metrics-proxy WARN scrape timeout exceeded for node/gpu-42```
evian: that handshake error is suspicious — did we rotate certs last night for kubelets?
liam: yes cert rotation ran on eu control-plane at 03:00 UTC but rollout was gradual. looks like prometheus-sidecar didn't pick up the new CA. sidecar logs show cert verification failures and then OOM from retry storms
aria: because sidecar was down, we lost both prometheus metrics and traces. autoscaler fell back to "no data -> assume zero" policy which caused routing to think region drained. The routing layer kept the region in pool but didn't actively shift because the failover policy requires explicit capacity alarm
evian: ops-bot created incident INC-20260317-17 and tagged oncall. I'll manually shift traffic for critical routes to us-west-1 while we remediate :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Incident INC-20260317-17 created and assigned to oncall (evan). Playbook: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-20260317-17
maya: short-term plan: 1) liam to push patched prometheus-sidecar image with backoff + fixed CA mount. 2) aria to backfill missing metrics from logs (node exporter and inference logs) and tag dashboards. 3) evan to run manual route-shift for heavy customers and verify SLA workarounds. 4) add temporary alert to routing when autoscaler returns no-data for >1m
liam: starting canary rollout of sidecar image now. command: ```kubectl -n monitoring set image ds/prometheus-sidecar prometheus-sidecar=registry.redwood/monitoring/sidecar:patch-20260317```. will monitor memory and TLS errors
aria: I'll kick off a logs->metrics backfill job to reconstruct GPU utilization for 10:00-10:30. also creating an eval to verify autoscaler logic won't assume zero when scrapers are missing
evian: doing the manual route shift now: switching critical routes off eu-central for 5m then watch for failover regressions. will post status
maya: follow-up actions (postmortem TODOs): - add synthetic scrape pings for metrics-proxy and kubelet so we never lose the entire scrape pipeline - make autoscaler more resilient: prefer recent last-known values for 2m instead of default to zero - ensure sidecar runs with memory limit + OOMKill prevention and proper CA mount validation - add runbook steps for manual traffic shift and emergency routing override
liam: can we also add a polling fallback where if prometheus sidecar is down we query node-exporter directly? that's quicker to implement than changing autoscaler logic
aria: agree. I'll own the fallback path and dashboard changes. liaise with liam for direct scrape policy
evian: traffic shift completed and customer-impact mitigation in place. monitoring shows queue lengths dropping in us-west. will keep incident open until backfill and sidecar rollout are green
maya: thanks everyone. please add brief notes to INC-20260317-17 thread for audit. we'll schedule a 30min postmortem tomorrow 09:00 UTC to lock the fixes
ops-bot: INC-20260317-17 status updated: mitigation in progress. assignees: liam, aria, evan, maya
